speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It provides the regulatory framework to keep the casinos free from criminal influence, ensure that gambling is conducted honestly and minimise the harms from gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The CCA also helps to ensure that the Integrated Resorts (IRs) make a positive contribution to our economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Other gambling activities that are not related to the casinos are regulated under a separate piece of legislation – the Gambling Control Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Taken together, the Casino Control Act and the Gambling Control Act help to ensure that gambling is well-regulated in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today's amendments are related to the regulation of the two casinos in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Singapore's approach to regulating casinos have worked well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This proportion has been stable over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The casino operators have not committed any significant breaches of gaming-related requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Since then, there have been changes to consumer preferences and gaming technology.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, we see new ways of gambling in overseas casinos including gambling using off-the-shelf mobile devices, such as tablets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our legislative framework must remain relevant and be responsive to these changes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has worked with the Ministry of Social and Family Development and the Ministry of Trade and Industry to review the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This Bill is the outcome of our review.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, the Gambling Regulatory Authority (GRA) approves all casino games, gaming machines and chips that are used in a casino.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This ensures that casino gambling is conducted honestly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To future-proof these approval regimes, clause 3 of the Bill amends three aspects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, it expands the scope of gambling activities that GRA can regulate in the casinos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, GRA is empowered to regulate games of chance offered by the casinos, such as table games and games on gaming machines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We propose to empower GRA to regulate all forms of gambling in the casinos, including betting and lotteries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Betting is distinct from games of chance because the former involves placing a stake on the outcome of a process, such as betting on a football competition or a horse race.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Lotteries are also distinct, as the distribution of prizes is dependent on chance, for example, the random drawing of lots in TOTO.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, clause 3 empowers GRA to approve gaming software.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, the GRA approves casino gaming machines comprising both the software and hardware components.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, manufacturers of gaming machines are increasingly developing gaming software independently from the hardware.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This amendment allows the GRA to approve gaming software on its own, for example, gaming software that is deployed on off-the-shelf mobile devices, such as tablets.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, clause 3 empowers the GRA to prescribe any wagering instrument to be used as chips for casino gambling, such as virtual credits, if the GRA assesses them to be suitable in the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The next set of amendments relates to the approval of manufacturers and suppliers of casino gaming machines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In recent years, the GRA has observed that for any particular gaming machine, there could be multiple manufacturers and suppliers for individual parts of the machine because of outsourcing arrangements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our policy intent is to regulate the entity that has overall control of the design or production of the gaming machines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 30 updates and streamlines the approval process, to only require approvals for such an entity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Other manufacturers and suppliers will no longer require GRA's approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The third set of amendments pertains to the main shareholders, controllers and substantial shareholders of the casinos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Only approved persons are allowed to take on these positions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are required to seek approval for acquisition and disposal of shares exceeding specific thresholds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This ensures that persons with control over the casinos are suitable persons and there is no undesirable influence over the casinos' operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill enhances the approval regime for such persons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, for the main shareholdings regime, clause 4 transfers the powers related to the approval of associated divestments and acquisitions, from the GRA to the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The main shareholders are accountable for the development of the IRs and their long-term commitments in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Their divestments and acquisitions are currently approved by the GRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Our view is that the Minister for Home Affairs is better-placed to balance whole-of-Government considerations and make these decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, for controllers and substantial shareholders, clause 17 transfers the related powers from the Minister for Home Affairs to the GRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These include, the powers to approve persons as controllers and substantial shareholders or to exempt them from any requirement under the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These decisions are currently made by the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: That said, we will allow persons to submit appeals on GRA's decisions to the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, clause 15 tightens the criteria for identifying associates under the controlled shareholdings regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, other than the corporate entity with controlled shareholdings in the casinos, all its related corporations are also subject to GRA's approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This would include related corporations that do not exercise influence or control over the casino operators, such as sister companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, for consistency with the Companies Act, we will tighten the criteria for identifying associates and ensure that only corporations that are able to exercise influence or control over the casino operators will be subject to GRA's approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fourth set of amendments clarifies the Evaluation Panel's ability to assess the tourism and economic impact of the IRs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Evaluation Panel provides an independent opinion to the GRA on the ability of the IR to fulfil its economic obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The GRA takes this into consideration when evaluating the application or renewal of a casino licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Evaluation Panel considers several factors, such as how the IRs compare to industry standards and whether they meet prevailing market demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 6 of the Bill clarifies in law that the Evaluation Panel may also take into consideration an IR's ability to meet future industry standards and market demand, in addition to prevailing standards and demand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This can be and is already being done today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: What this amendment does is to expressly state in law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Next, let me address the amendments to tighten the regulation of casinos and licensees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Even though casino-related crime remains low, we continually review and update our offences regime to deter crime and protect the integrity of gaming operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, clause 80 makes it an offence to withdraw bets after the result of a game is known.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, it is an offence under the CCA for casino patrons to place a bet in a casino after the result of a game is known, but the CCA is silent on the withdrawal of a bet after the result of a game is known.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, the Police have had to use provisions in other laws, such as the Penal Code, to deal with these cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This amendment will right-site the offence under the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, clause 79 makes it an offence to record non-card games in the casinos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is currently an offence to record cards dealt in the course of gaming.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, the Police have had to deal with such cases as an act of cheating at play under the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This amendment will expand the current offence to cover the recording of non-card games.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, clause 82 makes it an offence for any person to destroy or falsify documents, knowing that the document is required to be produced under the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, it is an offence for a person to destroy or falsify a document which he is required to submit to the GRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, the offence does not cover any other person who handles or has access to the same document, should they destroy or falsify it knowing that the document is required by the GRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This amendment will ensure that such persons can also be taken to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill also strengthens our ability to prosecute an excluded person, otherwise known as an EP, for entering a casino.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: With the exception of a self-excluded person, it is currently an offence for an EP to enter, remain or take part in gaming in a casino.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To make out an offence, the GRA has to prove that the EP was aware of his exclusion status when he entered the casino.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, an EP who had breached a Visit Limit could claim that he had miscounted his visits even though he was aware of his Visit Limit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This places the responsibility on an individual to ensure that he is not excluded before entering or when remaining in the casino where there are circumstances in which the individual ought reasonably to know that he is an EP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This means that an EP who had breached a Visit Limit and claims that it was because he had miscounted his visits would now be liable for an offence for entering or remaining in the casinos, since he ought reasonably to know when he would exceed his Visit Limit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The casino operators are expected to conduct their business operations in an ethical and credible manner, and to implement good corporate governance practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, whether the casino operator conducts business in a manner which is unethical or will bring discredit to casino gambling in Singapore; and second, whether the casino operator has poor corporate governance practices or weak internal controls.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This could include, disregarding whistle-blowing reports which allege employee misconduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Next, clauses 10, 26 and 35 empower the GRA to take disciplinary action against a former licensee for a regulatory breach, if the disciplinary action had commenced prior to the lapse of the licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This applies to all licensees under the CCA, including the casino operators, special employees, international market agents and international market agent representatives.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This amendment will ensure that no licensee evades punishment for contravening regulatory requirements, simply due to the lapse of his licence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the Personal Data Protection Act, a casino operator is currently not allowed to share the personal data of a patron directly with another casino operator without the patron's consent.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, when one casino operator assesses that a patron poses a high-risk of money laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing, the patron's personal data can be shared with the other casino operator, only through the GRA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This arrangement is operationally inefficient and impedes the casino operators from taking timely actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To address this, clause 47 empowers the GRA to require the casino operators to directly share information of patrons with each other, instead of going through the GRA, for the purposes of tackling money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The GRA will impose measures to safeguard patron information.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I now turn to the amendments to strengthen the protection for vulnerable individuals and their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, the National Council on Problem Gambling, otherwise known as the NCPG, administers Exclusions and Visit Limits to protect vulnerable groups of people and minimise the impact of problem gambling.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is an offence for an individual to breach an Exclusion by Law, a Third Party Exclusion Order or Visit Limit imposed by NCPG; or a Family Exclusion Order imposed by NCPG upon application by the individual's family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, a breach of a Family Visit Limit imposed upon application by the individual's family does not constitute an offence today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Currently, when there is a change in circumstances for an individual on an Exclusion Order or Visit Limit, the NCPG is only empowered to revoke the existing Exclusion Order or Visit Limit, before imposing a new Exclusion Order or Visit Limit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This process usually takes a period of one to two months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: During this period, the individual is not protected by any safeguard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 75 streamlines the process and allows the NCPG to immediately substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit, and vice versa.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As an illustration, this amendment will allow the NCPG to substitute a Visit Limit with an Exclusion Order seamlessly, to protect the individual by imposing a more stringent safeguard, if necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is to regularise the collection of casino entry levies between 4 April and 7 May this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The casino entry levy was introduced in 2008 as a social safeguard to deter casual and impulse gambling among Singaporean residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As part of the Government's commitment to keep problem gambling under control, we increased the casino entry levies on 4 April 2019 for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents from $100 to $150 for the daily levy, and from $2,000 to $3,000 for the annual levy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Government also introduced a five-year moratorium on the casino entry levies, as part of our negotiations with the casino operators on their reinvestment plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This was operationalised via the Casino Control (Variation of Entry Levies) Order 2019, which was valid for five years up to 3 April 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It has always been the Government's intent to maintain the higher entry levies beyond the five-year moratorium period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In other words, it was always the intent to renew the 2019 order upon its expiry rather than to allow the rate to revert to the lower one after the five-year period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, MHA overlooked the expiry of the 2019 Order and the entry levies reverted to the previous lower rates on 4 April 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: MHA acted immediately to remedy this when the issue was brought to our attention.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On 8 May 2024, MHA restored in law the daily levy to $150 and the annual levy to $3,000.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This was operationalised via the Casino Control (Variation of Entry Levies) Order 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is in line with the Government's policy intent for introducing the higher entry levy rates in 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We have tightened our processes to avoid this happening again.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: I would now like to speak in Mandarin, with your indulgence, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In Mandarin):   Next, I will outline in Mandarin the key proposals in the Bill that will affect casino patrons.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Although casino-related crime remains low, we continually review and update our offences regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This ensures that our laws continue to deter casino-related crime and protect the integrity of gaming operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill will, thus, introduce new offences in the CCA.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In particular, it will be an offence to withdraw bets after the result of a game is known and to record non-card games in the casinos.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill also strengthens our ability to prosecute an excluded person for entering a casino.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, there are amendments to strengthen the protection for vulnerable individuals and their families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, the NCPG administers Exclusion Orders and Visit Limits to protect vulnerable groups of people and minimise the impact of problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is a stark contrast when compared to the findings of a January 2024 report published by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, which reported a proliferation of organised crime in the rest of Southeast Asia due to the casino industries in the region.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The United Nations (UN) report also highlighted various trends in illegal gambling activities, including the increasing popularity of illegal online casinos using cryptocurrencies and other forms of virtual tokens in an attempt to evade local law enforcement.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A loot box is inherently gambling disguised in the form of a game.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the future, games could incorporate the concept of loot boxes and virtual tokens to allow players to gamble for a large sum of the token, which could then be converted into money through a roundabout manner.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In an article published just last month in The Guardian that examined the relationship between online gaming and gambling addiction, the experts interviewed said that research shows that children who play games with loot boxes are much more likely to experience gambling problems when they enter adulthood.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This could be because the odds in these games are better, causing them to think that they will have the same likelihood of success in the online gaming world.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that MHA can study this in our local context and examine if we need to take a tougher stance on regulating loot boxes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While we provide NCPG with the operational flexibility to protect vulnerable individuals, we must also ensure that there is an avenue of appeal should the individual disagree with the NCPG's decision.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond the Bill's proposals, I hope that we can widen our suite of enforcement tools to prevent vulnerable individuals from receiving unsolicited gambling advertisements.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Whenever there is a big global sporting event, such as the recent resumption of the English Premier League, it is common to receive unsolicited text messages encouraging a person to place big bets on unlicensed betting websites.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Advertisements that are programmatically pushed to viewers on social media also frequently feature online casinos and sports betting pages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I hope that the whole ecosystem, from telecommunications companies to social media companies, can lean in to aid both the GRA and NCPG to combat the issue of problem gambling and prevent vulnerable individuals from falling prey to gambling syndicates feeding on their gambling addiction.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As new forms of gambling arise through games and illegal websites, it is important that GRA is able to respond to these changes so that we ensure that illegal gambling and its ills will never take hold in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This is to be expected, in view of the high volumes of cash transactions that casinos undertake, whether in payments out to patrons or receiving cash in exchange for chips or other goods and services.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Among the 40 recommendations of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) on anti-money laundering measures, casinos are singled out for special mention.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At Recommendation 28, FATF advises that casinos should be subject to a comprehensive regulatory and supervisory regime that ensures that they have effectively implemented the necessary anti-money laundering and terrorist financing measures.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To that end, I see the Bill as another step towards this recommendation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On the provisions of the Bill, I wish to raise three points: first, on ownership of casino businesses; second, anti-money laundering measures; and third, the drastic increase in punishment for certain offences.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Later in this debate, my party colleague Sengkang Member of Parliament Louis Chua will raise questions regarding gambling duties and casino tax rates, the challenge of technology and the retrospective amendment regarding casino entry levies.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: FATF's Recommendation 28 on casinos advises that competent authorities should take the necessary legal or regulatory measures to prevent criminals or their associates from holding or being the beneficial owner of a significant or controlling interest, holding a management function in, or being an operator of a casino.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Put simply, we need to prevent organised criminal syndicates from profiting from casino businesses and laundering illegal funds through them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Under the existing CCA, approval of changes in the main shareholders of casinos needs approval from the GRA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Under the Bill, it is proposed that approval of changes in the main shareholder be transferred from the GRA to the Minister for Home Affairs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On the other hand, the opposite is being done for changes in ownership that do not involve the main shareholder.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For those who are controllers and substantial shareholders, the Bill removes certain powers from the Minister and transfers them to the GRA.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Ministry has sought to explain the rationale for these changes.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As regards the main shareholders, the Ministry has argued that considerations about the main shareholder should rightly be with the Minister, who can take into account whole-of-Government considerations.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: As for controllers and substantial shareholders, it is said that the decisions involved are regulatory decisions with operational implications, which are more appropriately undertaken by the GRA rather than the Minister.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Ministry please elaborate on this and what has changed?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Next, I move to the specific changes to enhance anti-money laundering measures in casinos.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: These are seen in clauses 46 and 47 of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Under clause 46, the threshold amounts of money which would trigger customer due diligence obligations have been lowered.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In addition, there will be a new requirement for the casino operator to expressly consider making a suspicious transaction report.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This requirement will be triggered when casino operators do not proceed with the transaction with the patron, whether it is because they are unable to complete the customer due diligence measures satisfactorily or because the patron refuses to provide the necessary information.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This scheme will provide for information sharing of the contents of a suspicious transaction report to prescribed persons once the filer is notified by the GRA to do so.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In the media release on the Bill, MHA explained that this scheme will enable casino operators to share information directly with each other so that those in the industry can act more quickly to prevent money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Already under the current obligations, our casino operators have occasionally fallen short.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Another operator was investigated in Singapore and the United States four years ago into whether it had fully complied with anti-money laundering measures when allowing patrons to transfer monies amongst themselves, known as "third party transfers".

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The risks are further amplified in Singapore due to the high percentage of casino patrons from overseas.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: According to Singapore's Money Laundering Risk Assessment Report released in June this year, the majority of casino patrons are foreigners, which would mean, that in most cases, our agencies may have little or no background information about these individuals.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Of course, the effectiveness of these enhanced anti-money laundering measures lies not just in the design but in the implementation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Much work will be needed by casino operators to review standard operating procedures and systems and to train staff to understand their roles.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The GRA's role as regulator is critical, as it works with the casino operators to literally raise their game.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: What is the mischief the Government wishes to address with these enhanced punishments?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Have casino operators or other persons not been cooperative with the Ministry or the GRA, such as to warrant these changes?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is no mean task and I hope we will succeed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That said, I look forward to the Government's clarifications on my queries regarding the swap in the approving authorities for ownership changes and the introduction of harsher punishments.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, I agree that the amendment Bill to take steps to further deter casino-related crime and protect the integrity of gaming operations is a timely one.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Nonetheless, I will like to raise clarifications pertaining to three areas: one, on Family Visit Limit; two, on future-proofing regulations; and three, on sharing of information among casino operators.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A Family Visit Limit can be applied by family members to limit the number of times a person can enter a casino, if his or her gambling behaviour has caused harm to them, including financial and emotional distress, neglect of family responsibilities or relationship breakdowns.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, behind each of this breach can be a very broken family situation with severe debts and relational strains to the family members.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Currently, it is an offence to breach an Exclusion Order by Law, Third Party Exclusion Order, Third Party Visit Limit or Family Exclusion Order.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Bill proposed to criminalise violation of Family Visit Limit at Singapore casinos.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I support the principle of increasing penalties for deterrent, often, the families with members who are problem gamblers are usually already facing immense financial distress when they need to apply for such a Family Visit Limit on the problem gambling family member.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, can the Ministry clarify what will be the considerations when a fine is to be imposed or will a jail term be a better deterrent instead.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My concern is that the burden of the fine of $10,000 will usually fall onto the innocent family members, causing even more downward spiral in their financial situation, instead of the problem gambler himself or herself.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, penalties may also be increased for minors faking their ages to get into casinos.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I will like to ask, how many of such cases have occurred so far.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Again, will a probation sentence be more appropriate for this group of offenders instead of a high financial penalty, which most minors will not be able to afford to pay and the burden will again fall onto the rest of the family who are innocent of the offence.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, the proposed changes will also extend GRA's regulation of casino activities to cover betting and lotteries, beyond games of chance.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Bill will also allow gaming software, which can be deployed on mobile devices, to be approved by the GRA if the need arises.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This follows the GRA's observation of gaming machine manufacturers developing software, without the hardware, which can be used on off-the-shelf devices, such as tablets.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The GRA can also allow new betting instruments to be used as chips in casinos in future, such as virtual credits, under the proposed changes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To pre-empt future changes in the gambling landscape, the Bill will also expand the scope of activities that the GRA can regulate in the casinos to cover betting and lotteries.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While the GRA has clarified that there are currently no plans to allow casinos in Singapore to carry out such betting and lottery activities, will the provision have a reverse effect of casinos considering such activities within the legislative framework, leading to more gaming activities than what the authorities will foresee, instead, in the casinos.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, regarding the change that will allow the GRA to assess which instruments can be regarded as chips, I would like to clarify whether virtual assets, such as cryptocurrency, can later be deemed a type of betting instrument and controlled by GRA's approval and how is the GRA keeping up with the understanding and supervision of new betting instruments.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, the proposed changes to the law will allow the two casino operators in Singapore to share patrons' information with each other to tackle money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The operators are, currently, not allowed to share personal data directly with each other without patrons' consent, due to the Personal Data Protection Act.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Instead, the GRA needs to facilitate this exchange, which is mentioned by the Ministry as operationally inefficient and impedes the operators from acting quickly.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is in line with the efforts to tackle money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It also fits with Singapore's recent moves to best align with the guidelines of the FATF.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I agree with the amendments to enhance operational efficiency, I seek the Ministry's clarifications on how the process will be initiated by the casinos and what is the difference in timeline of information sharing compared to the current legislation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How would the GRA know if either casino has failed to initiate such important information sharing and what other surveillance or inspection measures does the GRA have, to identify such risky patrons in the two casinos?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As such, strengthening our casino control legislation will be a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As we continue to witness the growth and evolution of the gaming industry in Singapore and beyond, it is essential that we take decisive action to enhance the operational effectiveness of our regulatory regime, ensuring it can adapt to evolving challenges.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Most importantly, this Bill also seeks to strengthen protections for our most vulnerable groups: families, individuals at risk of addiction and those who could be disproportionately affected.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This is a necessary step toward balancing economic interests with our duty to safeguard the well-being of our society.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: On the topic of economic interests, I wish to, once again, raise the point I made during this year's Budget debate that in Singapore, betting taxes as a percentage of gross domestic product have been flat in past years at around 0.5%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Given that gambling duties have been unchanged since 2014, there is room to look into raising the relevant gambling duties as a means of supplementing fiscal revenues consistent with an approach of raising taxes on activities with negative externalities.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For casino taxes, while I am cognisant that these were raised in 2022, I would argue today as I did back then when we were debating the Gambling Duties Bill, that casino tax rates have much room to grow.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This would bring effective gaming tax rates to higher than 35%.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is especially important to place this call for an increase against the context of the two IRs here reporting very strong profitability in spite of the higher casino tax rates.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Further, Las Vegas Sands Corp continues to enjoy the highest EBITDA margins in Singapore at 51%, compared to 33% at its Macau operations, despite the higher casino tax rates and this would also have likely been higher than its Las Vegas properties which have since been divested.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Considering that casino licences are renewed with every three years, with the current term expiring in 2025, is there scope for the casino tax rates to be raised in the coming years?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Under the recent development agreements signed between the Government and the two casino licensees, what are the maximum casino tax rates that are specified and what are the terms and conditions required before these can be raised in future, assuming the expansion plans of both IRs are completed on schedule?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Is the Government constrained in its ability to raise casino and gambling duties in the next few years?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Second, I understand that the Bill seeks to provide for advances in technology and changes to the way gambling and casino operators are carried out.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I note that under clause 3, the definition of a "gaming program" is inserted, which refers to a software application designed to be used with an electronic device other than a gaming machine to play a casino game or participate in any other form of gambling.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In its press release, MHA noted that this was in response to manufacturers of gaming machines developing software, which can be deployed on off-the-shelf mobile devices such as tablets.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I struggle to see how the GRA can restrict the deployment of such gaming software within the casino premises only, should it be approved.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As it is today and as I have highlighted in my speech in March 2022, illegal online gambling remains a key problem regardless of whether official gaming software is being deployed by gaming manufacturers.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: When I tried to visit one of the popular online gambling websites of yesteryear, I was greeted by a notice by the GRA saying in bold red font, "Access Blocked", followed by "You have attempted to access an illegal gambling site hosted by an unlicensed gambling service provider.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Singapore Pools is the only licensed online gambling operator in Singapore." However, a simple google search of "online gambling" throws up numerous websites, listing down all the different online gambling portals in Singapore, supposedly.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The top link even includes a list of "the best Singapore online casino sites", with the self-styled "gambling expert" claiming that "gambling at online casino in Singapore is becoming more and more popular as the years go by.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Because of this, it probably comes as no surprise to learn that there are now loads of options for players to choose from".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I appreciate that while a key part of our strategy to combat illegal online gambling is our blocking measures for illegal online gambling websites and that, yes, no blocking measures are foolproof, but could we better harness technology to stay ahead of the curve and make it prohibitive to access such online gambling portals in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Considering that a person convicted of gambling with unlicensed gambling service providers is liable for a fine of up to $10,000 or a jail term of up to six months or both, are there corresponding penalties for operators of unlicensed gambling service providers, regardless of where they are domiciled if they are offering such services to users in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In its press release on 6 August 2024, MHA stated that: "It was always the Government's intent to maintain the higher entry levies beyond the five-year period.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, MHA had overlooked the expiry of the 2019 Order".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Curiously, section 2 of the 2019 Order itself merely stated that "The entry levies specified in section 116(1) of the Act are replaced, for the period starting on 4 April 2019 and ending on 3 April 2024, as follows...".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: There is no indication of the Government's intention after the moratorium – if levies are going to be higher, lower or maintained – except that this levy is to be in place for exactly five years.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Less than a year ago, my Sengkang colleague Assoc Prof Jamus Lim spoke eloquently in this House of the importance of not treating retrospective applications of the law lightly and how if we routinely amend laws and apply them after the fact, then, we erode the very stability of the rule of law.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong also appeared to agree with this principle and said that and I quote, "Backdating, as Assoc Prof Jamus Lim correctly said, should be done sparingly.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is really the exception rather than the norm and we do it very, very rarely.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Because backdating upsets expectations and prejudices individuals who rely on the existing law".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: MHA stated in its August press release that "we have tightened our processes to avoid a repeat of such an incident".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: But such an incident involving the backdating of laws to fix a mistake should not be treated lightly.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: When confronted with this issue, one approach is to accept that a mistake was made by the Ministry and enact legislation prospectively, given that it is quite clear in my opinion that there are Singaporeans and PRs who are prejudiced.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Whatever one's views are towards those who visit casinos is quite secondary to the principle of the rule of law we are trying to uphold in this country.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Allow me to conclude in Mandarin, Mdm Deputy Speaker.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Firstly, although we often say "a little gambling can be fun", the reality is that more often "nine out of ten gamblers lose".

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Therefore, I believe that while pursuing economic benefits, we should also safeguard social welfare and continuously strengthen our protection of vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In an era where online gambling is rampant, blocking certain sites cannot be completely watertight.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Can we utilise technology to stay ahead and effectively control gambling issues?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This would not only supplement fiscal revenue but also help curb the social ills brought about by gambling activities.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Thirdly, the Prime Minister has said that retrospective legislation should be treated with caution and only used as a last resort.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This includes enhancing protection against money laundering and criminal conduct, as well as strengthening internal controls and corporate governance for casinos.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: The obvious and direct harm of problem gambling is that it causes financial harm, which can spiral into debt accumulation, asset loss and even bankruptcy.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: While some may find some joy and thrill from a momentary, once-off gamble and win, the truth is that it is a fine line and easily a slippery slope towards habitualised problematic gambling, to the extent where financial losses are compounded further from an inability to walk away or exercise self-control, where social relationships are torn from the unfounded preoccupation for the next winning gamble, a loss of trust and an inability to fulfil personal, family and vocational responsibilities and where chasing losses and desperation can contribute to behaviours with legal consequences.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: A person seized with problem gambling is not only at risk of being impacted with mental and physical health concerns but, as covered by the Bill, families and loved ones are at risk and vulnerable to the extended harm a person's problematic gambling habits can bring.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This is so much so that where it was formerly known as pathological gambling, the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (DSM) of Mental Disorders, in its fifth edition, DSM-5, has re-categorised it as gambling disorder.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: So, from pathological gambling to gambling disorder, to become the first recognised non-substance behavioural addiction in DSM.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: This was also to reflect growing evidence that gambling behaviours activate reward systems in the brain similar to those activated by drugs of abuse and alcohol and can produce behavioural symptoms comparable to those produced by substance abuse.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I hope this tells us that we can never let our guard down when it comes to the harms of gambling and, by extension, that the amendments, through this Bill, to the Casino Control Act, must keep pace with any emerging evidence of harm that gambling and casino operations can potentially contribute to an individual and his/her family.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: With that as a preamble, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I have several queries that I hope the Ministry can address.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: It appears that the distinction is drawn only when there is a wager of money or casino chips.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I would argue that the fundamental harm and psychological impact comes from participating in the game of chance itself, whether wagered on money, chips or otherwise.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: In the context of a casino, such a promotional game is a precursor and an encouragement to the actual casino gambling and casino game itself.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: My view is that a promotional game in the casino should be treated the same as per any casino game, without having to distinguish it and suggesting that it is of a lesser harm under the Act.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Within the changes to the Bill, this distinction is only made under Part 1, section 2 of the Act under the subheading of Interpretation.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: However, practically, under the relevant sections for Exclusion Orders, this harm is, indeed, recognised as with the same weight and grievance regardless whether they be promotional or casino games and all manner of games, promotional games inclusive, are prohibited.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Under current practice or regulations, is there a prescribed distance as to where ATMs can or cannot be to a casino?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: I ask this because within close locality of, for example, the Marina Bay Sands casino as an example, an online search suggests the availability of ATMs of different banks located close within the vicinity outside the casino.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Are there similar legal provisions for locality of ATMs at other gambling type of establishments, for example, Singapore Pool lottery outlets?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: And in the era of online payments and transactions, does the proximity prohibition of ATMs remain an appropriate and effective deterrent at all?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Practically speaking, a 24-hour period may encourage a person to gamble comfortably over two calendar days depending on the start of the 24-hour window.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Fourth, also on a related note to the previous point, regarding Exclusion Orders in general, for a person who is already imposed a Visit Limit due to known problematic gambling behaviours, I wonder if he or she should still be granted the same privilege of a continuous 24 hours per visit as someone who is not on such a Visit Limit.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: When considered under an Exclusion Order and a prescribed Visit Limit, can each visit be restricted further to one entry and exit only, or be restricted to a specified lesser number of hours, rather than for the person imposed on a Visit Limit be allowed to spend a continuous period of 24 hours at the casino just like any other person?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Fifth, regarding family exclusion and third-party Exclusion Orders, could the Ministry perhaps give an update as to whether these continue to be effective and whether the intent of such Exclusion Orders is met and fulfilled in that it supports the recovery of the individual and has prevented further harm?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member)
text: Notwithstanding my comments and clarifications, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I rise in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Gambling addiction has long been a matter of social concern and can destroy lives of individuals, families and friends.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In my growing up years back in the 1960s, I became aware of relatives with gambling issues and recall how this distanced them from family and, in turn, often, family from them.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I was then too young to fully appreciate the realities.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: Though I do recall with some detail that there was a constant search for money to pay debts, including dealing with the demands of debt collectors, sometimes these were quite intimidating.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: When we awarded the two casino licences, there was understandable concern over the social impact, in particular, for the vulnerable and potentially those who had worked hard to build up savings that could be placed at risk.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I acknowledge the various initiatives in response to the concerns and directed to minimise the consequences on various groups.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: I am encouraged that the relevant authorities constantly review protection for individuals affected by or at risk of problem gambling.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, I do support the broader objectives of this Bill to continue to stay relevant to the changing landscape.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill will improve the effectiveness of our casino regulatory regime, tighten the regulation of casinos and licensees and strengthen protection for vulnerable groups.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MHA shared that our regulatory regime has worked well and these amendments are part of MHA’s regular reviews of our laws.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that we are proactively reviewing our laws to ensure our legislative framework is able to meet anticipated developments in the gambling landscape.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarification to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first point is on the responsible entity or individual for approving changes in main shareholders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In its press release, MHA explained its rationale: “The Minister for Home Affairs would be better placed than the GRA to take into account whole-of-Government considerations, in deciding whether to approve divestments and acquisitions relating to main shareholdings.” Can the Minister of State clarify what whole-of-Government considerations will the Minister for Home Affairs take into account when approving divestments and acquisitions of main shareholders?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I ask this question because the GRA has long been entrusted to make complex assessments on long-term viability and economic prospects when deciding on casino licence applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is unclear why the GRA is now a poor fit for making considerations about main shareholders.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How are considerations related to main shareholders different from considerations that the GRA must already take into account when approving casino licences?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State provide some examples of whole-of-Government considerations that the Minister for Home Affairs is better placed than the GRA to take into account?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second point is on the removal of the requirement for a hearing before Exclusion or Visit Limit Orders are made.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The effect of these changes is that the NCPG or one of its committees does not always need to hold a hearing for applications.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The amended provisions still require the NCPG or its committees to give a person a reasonable opportunity to object to an application for an order against him or her or to make representations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State explain the rationale for removing the requirement for a hearing?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister of State clarify whether following the amendments, by default, the NCPG or committee will not hold a hearing for applications?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Are there situations where the NCPG or a committee may nonetheless decide to hear an application?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If so, what are the types of cases where a hearing may be deemed necessary?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final point is on the powers of the NCPG to substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit, and vice versa.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 166A lists the types of substitutions that can be made and sets out the tests for when the NCPG may make a substitution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This process usually takes one or two months.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that it is no longer a requirement for hearings to be conducted, can the Minister of State explain how the NCPG will obtain all evidence necessary to determine whether a substitution is appropriate?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While the amendments require the NCPG to provide the party concerned a reasonable opportunity to make representations on the relevant matter, since a hearing is no longer required, there is a higher risk that the NCPG may not hear from a party.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Where a party does not make representations, can the Minister of State share if the NCPG will proactively request material or evidence from the relevant agencies or individuals to ensure it has the full information to make the determination?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They raised important questions which I will now address.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First, on enhancing the operational effectiveness of our casino regulatory regime.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun asked about the need to distinguish a promotional game from casino gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Promotional games are a form of casino promotion.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Compared to the casino games, they pose a lower risk of gambling harm as they do not involve a wager.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We use therefore a lighter hand to regulate promotional games.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Although GRA’s approval is still required before a casino operator conducts promotional games, certain regulatory requirements which are imposed on casino games, are not imposed on the promotional games.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, there is no need for the promotional games to be conducted by licensed casino employees.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked if the amendment to expand the scope of gambling activities in casinos that the GRA can regulate, to include betting and lotteries, would inadvertently encourage casino operators to consider offering such activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are already casinos in other countries that offer betting and lotteries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With this amendment, it will be clear that a casino operator must get GRA’s approval before offering any new gambling activity, including betting and lotteries.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA has not received any requests from the casino operators to offer betting or lottery-based products.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Should they do so, the GRA will carefully consider the proposal, including law and order and social concerns.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua raised the issue of how the GRA will be able to ensure that the deployment of gaming software is restricted to the casino premises should it be approved by the GRA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA intends to allow the casino operators to offer gaming only on mobile devices provided by the casino operators and within the casino.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They must demonstrate how they would ensure that the gaming software cannot be used outside the casino, for instance, using geofencing technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked if virtual assets such as cryptocurrency are within the scope of wagering instruments that the GRA would be able to prescribe as chips for casino gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The amendment empowers the GRA to prescribe any wagering instrument to be used as chips for casino gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intent of this is to future-proof the regime to allow for new modes such as cashless gaming.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: An example is where a patron may place wagers at either the gaming tables or gaming machines by drawing down virtual credits directly from his cashless gaming account or e-wallet.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng and Ms Sylvia Lim asked how we arrived at the assessments that the Minister for Home Affairs would be better placed than the GRA to approve divestments and acquisitions relating to main shareholders and that the GRA would be better placed than the Minister to manage decisions relating to controllers and substantial shareholders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The main shareholders regime is the principal upstream lever for the Government to decide who should be allowed to operate the IRs and the casinos within.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The current main shareholders for Marina Bay Sands and Resorts World Sentosa are Las Vegas Sands Corp and Genting Singapore Limited respectively.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are operators whom we have assessed are aligned with Singapore's strategic objectives for the IRs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will also bring it in line with the existing policy where it is the Minister who decides on the entity to be designated as the main shareholder of the casino operator in the first place.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Decisions relating to controllers and substantial shareholders, however, have different considerations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The key is to ensure that they do not have undesirable backgrounds so as to ensure that the operation of the casino will be free from criminal influence or infiltration.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When the Casino Control Act was introduced in 2006, we took reference from the Banking Act, where it is the Minister who approves changes to controllers and substantial shareholders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Given the context of the Casino Control Act, which has the concept of a main shareholder, unlike financial institutions under the Banking Act, we assess that decisions relating to non-main shareholders can be made by the GRA and that the GRA is well placed to do so.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Since taking up the mantle of Singapore's casino regulator in 2008, the GRA has done well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is evidenced by the low crime rate and problem gambling rate in casinos.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will now deal with the questions on tightening the regulation of casinos and licensees.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked how information sharing between the casino operators will be initiated, what would be the time difference for this proposed information sharing process as compared to the current process and how the GRA would know if either casino operator has failed to initiate such a process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, where an operator has made a suspicious transaction report on a customer and has declined to establish a relationship with him or her.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA conducts regular and ad hoc inspections on the casinos.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If it detects any non-compliance with regulatory requirements, including the failure to share necessary information with the other operator, it will investigate and take appropriate enforcement action.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked what other surveillance or inspection measures the GRA has in place to identify patrons who may pose a high risk of money laundering, terrorism financing or proliferation financing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Casino operators are already required to have in place a framework for the prevention of money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing, which includes identifying and managing high-risk patrons and mitigating the risks associated with these patrons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The operators must take into consideration the profile and behaviour of patrons and establish risk and materiality thresholds for the identification of high-risk patrons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the impetus for imposing an imprisonment term for offences that were originally liable for only a fine.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Casino Control Act was last amended more than 10 years ago.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Since then, the Gambling Control Act, which brought together all non-casino gambling matters, has come into force, in 2022.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The prospect of an imprisonment term will also be a stronger deterrent against the commission of such offences.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will now deal with the questions on strengthening protection for vulnerable groups of people.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Keith Chua raised the issue of deploying more resources to prevent problem gambling and to protect vulnerable groups of people.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This includes extensive public education campaigns and initiatives and also funding social service agencies that offer gambling rehabilitation services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Chua also asked if the access points to the casinos can be reviewed to minimise exposure to unsuspecting visitors or minors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA imposes regulatory requirements to reduce public exposure to the casinos.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For instance, gaming areas cannot open directly into public spaces, visitors and guests should not have to walk through the casino in order to gain access to other IR facilities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are also other measures to limit the accessibility of casinos, including the entry levy regime and the minimum 21 years age restriction.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Taken together, our approach has generally worked well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to closely monitor the situation through NCPG's regular Gambling Participation Survey.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun asked about the effectiveness of Exclusion Orders and if there should be further restrictions imposed on persons on Visit Limits.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Social safeguards, including Exclusion Orders and Visit Limits, have played a key role in ensuring that problem gambling in Singapore remains under control.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A person who is financially distressed will be subject to an Exclusion Order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Visit Limit is generally imposed on less financially vulnerable persons, together with other safeguards in place in the casinos, to help them control their gambling on the ground.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to monitor the effectiveness of our social safeguards.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will take the Member's suggestions into account if there is a future need to tighten them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Keith Chua suggested allowing parents to apply for an exclusion for their children who are below 21 years of age.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A breach of a Family Exclusion Order is an offence and hence, the family should only apply for it when there is evidence of harm caused by gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For parents who are concerned about minors under their care, they should educate them on the harms of gambling and not to start gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Parents can encourage their children to apply for self-exclusion when they turn 21.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun also suggested having a mechanism for doctors or psychiatrists to report problem gamblers to the NCPG for consideration of a Third Party Exclusion Order, likening it to how doctors are obliged to report any illicit drug use today.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Problem gambling, unlike drug abuse, is not a crime.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There is therefore less ground to override patient-doctor confidentiality and require medical professionals to report individuals whom they suspect to be problem gamblers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nevertheless, medical professionals should encourage such individuals to exercise personal responsibility and avoid gambling beyond their means.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They should also encourage the individuals to seek help, including through channels like the NCPG Helpline or Webchat or to apply for self-exclusion or Voluntary Visit Limits to help them control their gambling habit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun asked whether an existing Donee or Deputy of an incapacitated person should continue his role if he or she is issued with an Exclusion Order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Individuals can be issued an Exclusion Order for many reasons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The public can whistle-blow to the Office of Public Guardian on alleged misconduct by Donees or Deputies, including misconduct that may have arisen as a result of their being issued Exclusion Orders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In response to Dr Harun's other questions relating to Donees and Deputies, the Minister for Social and Family Development can appoint suitable persons to apply for a Family Exclusion Order for the incapacitated person.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Suitable persons may include Lasting Power of Attorney Donees or Court-appointed Deputies.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked when a fine would be meted out against a person who has breached his or her Family Visit Limit and when a jail term would be imposed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She raised concerns that the burden of a fine would usually fall onto the family members, causing them further financial burden.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In considering the punishment, the GRA will assess the facts and circumstances and consult the Attorney-General's Chambers, who will make the final decision.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Once the matter is in Court, the Court will assess and mete out the appropriate punishment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng had a few questions on how NCPG's Committee of Assessors makes its decisions on an Exclusion Order or Visit Limit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Bill will simply provide the Committee with the option to not convene a hearing if it already has sufficient evidence to assess the case, including documents which the respondent has submitted, or if the respondent has consented to the Exclusion Order or Visit Limit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On Mr Ng’s other questions on the empowering of NCPG to substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit or vice versa, let me elaborate on the appeal and revocation process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Today, the respondent is already required to provide supporting evidence to help the NCPG make a decision and the NCPG may request additional information.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
