text: The NCPG will use this information to determine whether the initial order remains appropriate, or where there are changes to the respondent's circumstances, whether it is more appropriate to substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit or vice versa.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked if there will be changes to the channels through which respondents can express their disagreement with NCPG’s decision on Exclusion Orders and Visit Limits.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Individuals who disagree with NCPG’s decision may appeal against it, or apply to vary or revoke their Exclusion Order or Visit Limit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The enhanced operational flexibility to allow the NCPG to substitute an Exclusion Order with a Visit Limit and vice versa, will be incorporated into NCPG’s workflows.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling noted the increase of the fine for minors refusing to give particulars or using false evidence of age to enter casinos, from $1,000 to $10,000, and asked if a probation order would be more appropriate.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With a financial penalty, she is concerned that the financial burden would fall on the family.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She also asked about the number of cases of minors who had managed to enter the casinos by providing false evidence of age.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A minor’s failure to comply with the request by an authorised person such as a Police officer or the GRA inspector to provide his or her particulars shows defiance and prevents the officers from carrying out their duties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Also, the use of false evidence of age by a minor to enter casinos is essentially deceit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are serious offences which we must deter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we are increasing the penalties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The increase will also ensure parity with the penalties for similar offences under the Gambling Control Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We note Ms Ng's point that the family would likely end up having to pay the fine on behalf of the minor.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is the case even today, including for other offences outside the Casino Control Act and the Gambling Control Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The family is responsible for the minor and it cannot completely absolve themselves from the minor's misdemeanours.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So far, the GRA has not prosecuted any minor for failing to provide particulars or giving false evidence of age.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But in the event that a case is prosecuted and a minor is found guilty by the Court, the Court will consider all available orders, including probation, taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will move on to the other issues and suggestions from Members.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about casino tax rates and noted that the rates were raised recently in March 2022, through the Gambling Duties Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As this falls outside the scope of this Bill, I will address this only briefly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was to provide the IRs with greater certainty, bolster the competitiveness and attractiveness of the IRs, as well as enhance the investors’ ability to raise funds for the IRs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This was important to the IRs, given the significant amount of investments that they would be committing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Since then, we revised the casino tax rates once, upon the expiry of the moratorium in 2022.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We introduced a tiered casino tax structure, with higher tax rates than before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The rates were also subjected to a 10-year moratorium.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The rates were set with a view to striking a balance between competitiveness and revenue.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will review the casino tax rates closer to the end of the moratorium.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun asked about the prohibition of ATMs within the boundaries of casinos and its effectiveness as a deterrent.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: ATMs are prohibited within the gambling venues of casinos and gaming machine rooms.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This creates a "break in play" and injects some inconvenience to the patron.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is to prevent them from having easy and instant access to additional funds for gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This restriction is still relevant today as there remains a sizeable proportion of patrons who gamble using cash.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not prescribe any minimum distance between the ATMs and the casinos.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA has imposed similar requirements for a "break in play" where electronic payments are used by casino patrons.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Dr Syed Harun also suggested the shortening of the validity period of an entry levy.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For now, we do not think that there is a need to increase the levies further or to reduce their validity period.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Melvin Yong raised the issue of illegal remote gambling activities and unsolicited gambling advertisements on social media platforms.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I mentioned in my speech earlier that the regulation of non-casino gambling activities is covered under the Gambling Control Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As these matters fall outside the scope of this Bill, I will address them very briefly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We take a strong enforcement approach against illegal gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: About one-third of the arrests were for remote gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The GRA carries out blocking of illegal online gambling websites and advertisements that can be accessed in Singapore, as well as payment services linked to illegal online gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, the Online Criminal Harms Act empowers the authorities to issue Directions to online service providers to restrict the exposure of Singapore users to criminal activities, including illegal gambling advertisements, on their platforms.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On Mr Yong’s suggestion regarding loot boxes, our current approach to regulating loot boxes is a balanced one.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It aims to safeguard against gambling inducement, rather than gaming.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to monitor the landscape closely.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yong would recall that earlier this year, MHA imposed new restrictions on the value of prizes for games at amusement centres and funfairs, because of the higher risk of gambling inducement when large prizes are offered.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Similarly, if we find that loot boxes are becoming a significant driver of gambling inducement, we will review our regulations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua asked about the penalties for operators providing unlicensed gambling services, regardless of where they are domiciled.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under the Gambling Control Act, the definition of remote gambling covers situations where the facilities are outside of Singapore, whether in part or in full.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: An illegal gambling operator is thus liable for an offence and faces the same penalties, even if he resides overseas, as long as the illegal gambling service is accessible by Singapore users.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But given the difficulties with enforcing this law against foreign operators, the GRA’s first recourse is to block such illegal online gambling websites.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Chua also talked about the regularisation of entry levies collected between 4 April and 7 May 2024.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The entry levies collected were in line with the higher levies that were imposed since 2019.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It was always the intent to continue the higher levies until such time that we assess that there is a need to further adjust the rates.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intent of the moratorium was to stipulate that the levies will not change during the five-year period.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The intent was for the rates to be at least maintained thereafter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I do not think that there were expectations that the rates would revert to the earlier lower rate after the five-year period.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have heard many in this House talk about their concerns about problem gambling.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I believe that more would be in support of the maintenance of levies imposed since 2019, rather than to lower the levies to what was first set in 2006, and which may inevitably end up encouraging more gamblers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That said, we are not treating this incident lightly.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have been upfront to acknowledge the issue and we have come to Parliament to validate the excess collections during this period.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Are there any clarifications from Members for the Minister of State?
